THIS ARCHIVE WITHDRAWS ITS OWN INFERENCE. From Orazio naming two sons Domenico, naming custom suggested his father was a Domenico Arena. Two Orazio Arena births at Scilla now say otherwise: act 10 of 1821 gives him a father GIUSEPPE (and the tree's own year, 1821, exactly), and act 1 of 1833 gives a different Orazio a father BONAVENTURA. Neither is a Domenico. The mistake was not the custom but the assumption behind it: the first child this archive had FOUND was not necessarily his FIRST child. The years 1850-1855 are unread, and a son Giuseppe in one of them would restore the custom exactly. Recorded as a candidate: ORAZIO ARENA b. 14 DECEMBER 1821, son of Giuseppe Arena and a Teresa. FURTHER EVIDENCE, BOTH WAYS: Orazio's earliest known child is a DAUGHTER, Teresa, born 17 October 1853. Custom names the first daughter for her paternal grandmother, and act 10 of 1821 makes Orazio's mother a Teresa -- which SUPPORTS the 1821 candidate. But that same act makes his father a Giuseppe, and Orazio's first son is Domenico, with 1852-1855 now read and no earlier son. The two halves disagree and the archive is not picking one.

recordSays: The Ellis Island manifest of 23 May 1899 states it outright: Giovanni Arena, 45, a sailor, sails to join 'BROTHER ROCCO, N. YORK, MULBERRY ST', and the six-year-old on the next line is entered not by surname but as 'NIECE, Anna Arena'. So Giovanni is Rocco Arena's brother and Anna is Rocco's daughter -- both stated on the document. HE IS IN THE TREE, and this row once said he was not: he is the Giovanni Arena the tree marries to Concetta Russo and dates to 1870. The missing people are his PARENTS. THE INDEX LINE AND THE ACT DISAGREE, AND THE DISAGREEMENT IS SETTLED. The 1854 Tavola reads «Arena Giovanni di Antonio e Arlotta ROSA, 20 April», and this archive repeated it and drew the wrong conclusion from it -- a ROSA Arlotta would be Serafina's sister, which would make the boy Rocco's COUSIN rather than his brother. The act itself, act 76, says SERAFINA and says the THIRTIETH of April, and the ages close it: Francesco Antonio was thirty-four in April 1854 to the month. The index is wrong. It is recorded here because an index this archive trusted produced a false relationship, and the next one might too.

Rosario Mazza and Anna Cassanite named a son Orazio for his grandfather, exactly as the naming custom predicts, and the export then recorded that son in both the parents and the children. The child link stands; the parent link is removed. His father remains the Orazio Mazza born 1883 at Piedimonte Etneo, son of Rosario Mazza and Leonarda.

treeSays: ANGELA CUPO, with no parents and no surname evidence
recordSays: ANGELA CRUPI, daughter of FRANCESCO CRUPI and MARIA VECCHIO. Her Queensland death registration of 10 January 1973 names both parents, and the Nudgee register interred her three days later in plot V-0116 beside her husband Rosario Mazza in V-0117. Born 1900 at Catania, died 1973 at Brisbane, which is exactly the woman the export holds. CUPO IS A GARBLING OF CRUPI, and this data does that often — «Lecota» for Nicotra and «Postamo» for Prostamo are both already on this page.
source: Queensland death registration 1973/B/38514, against the Nudgee Catholic cemetery register

kind: my own reading — a name in dispute
treeSays: Not in the tree at all; this archive published her as MARIA Paladino
recordSays: MARTA, most likely. Her son Domenico's birth act of 18 December 1816 -- written while she was in the next room, from her husband's own mouth -- reads «e da MAR-TA PALADINO, di anni trenta, sua moglie legittima», the name broken across a line with the second beginning plainly «ta». This archive first published her as MARIA, from the 1844 marriage Tavola. The act is contemporaneous and primary; the Tavola is an index compiled at the year's end, and THIS SERIES HAS ALREADY BEEN CAUGHT at exactly this -- the 1854 Tavola calls Serafina Arlotta «Rosa», and believing it briefly turned a brother into a cousin. AGAINST THAT, HONESTLY: the same Tavola entry gets the other mother right, «de Amico Maria», as her daughter's own birth act confirms. So the index is not uniformly careless and this is a reading, not a verdict. Another child of Candeloro Donato in the Scilla births of 1810-1830 would settle it.
source: Scilla, Nati 1816 atto 207, in Matrimoni processetti 1842-1845 fascicolo 20

kind: Missing people — AND THE END OF A LINE
recordSays: BORN ABOUT 1783 and a MARINARO -- thirty-three when he declared his son Domenico's birth on 18 December 1816. The first age this archive has ever had for him, and the last it will get: Scilla's civil registration begins in 1816, so his own birth and marriage are pre-civil, and his son Michele was born at MESSINA about 1814 where registration does not begin until 1820. HE IS WHERE THE SCILLA LINE STOPS, exactly as Pasquale Prostamo is where the Calabrian one does. He was still alive in July 1844 -- his son's marriage bundle carries no death certificate, which this series required when a parent had died.
source: Scilla, Nati 1816 atto 207, in Matrimoni processetti 1842-1845 fascicolo 20

kind: a document against a document — a surname in dispute
treeSays: Not in the tree; this archive publishes her as ANNA FAMA
recordSays: TWO RECORDS, TWO SURNAMES, AND NEITHER IS THE ORIGINAL. Domenico Ventrice's wife is named twice in this archive and not the same way. The CHANCERY'S CERTIFIED COPY OF 1849, made thirty-four years after his death and filed in his granddaughter's marriage bundle at Briatico, calls her ANNA FAMA. His son's own marriage act -- ZAMBRONE, 2 MARCH 1824, written in the town where Domenico died and only nine years after he died, from the groom's own statement -- calls her «LA FU ANNA MAROPOLI». THE 1824 ACT IS PREFERRED, for three reasons: it is nearer the event by twenty-five years, it was written in the right comune, and THE SAME 1849 COPY HAS ALREADY BEEN CAUGHT GETTING SOMETHING WRONG -- it crams two ages into one clause and this archive first read Domenico as fifty when he was fifty-eight. BUT NEITHER IS THE ACT ITSELF. THE VOLUME HAS NOW BEEN OPENED AND THE ORIGINAL IS NOT THERE. Zambrone's death register runs 1811, then 1812 ending with its own Tavola, then a title page -- and then 1822. THE YEARS 1813 TO 1821 ARE PHYSICALLY ABSENT and Domenico died in January 1815. SO THIS CANNOT BE SETTLED FROM ZAMBRONE'S OWN REGISTER. ONE THING DID CHANGE, AND IN MAROPOLI'S FAVOUR: the 1822 death Tavola of the same volume names a «fu Franc.co e Dom.ca MAROPOLI» as the parents of a Francesca Pungitori. AND IT IS NOT AN ISOLATED INSTANCE. Sweeping the death Tavole of 1822, 1823 and 1824 turns up MAROPOLI TWICE: as a parent's surname in 1822, and as GIUSEPPE MAROPOLI himself, an infant dead on 23 March 1824, son of Antonio and Marianna Colia. TWO INDEPENDENT ATTESTATIONS INSIDE TWO YEARS. So the reading «della fu Anna Maropoli» no longer needs defending AS A READING. What stays open is only which of two documents is right -- and that cannot be decided until Domenico Ventrice's own act is found, which needs the second copy of a register whose comune copy is missing these years. Work list row 59.
source: Zambrone, Matrimoni 1824 atto 2 and Morti 1822 Tavola; against Briatico, Matrimoni 1849, atto 1 (processetti)

kind: Missing people — A COUPLE NEVER HAD
treeSays: Not in the tree, and not in this archive either until today
recordSays: CATERINA CICHELLO'S PARENTS. Her marriage act of 2 March 1824 at Zambrone names her «figlia DEL FU FRANCESCO e DELLA FU VITTORIA MOLLO» -- both already dead when she married at twenty-six. She is the great-great-great-grandmother of Mia and Rocco, and her parents were the oldest completely unknown couple on the Calabrian side. The act also gives her a birthplace, ZAMBRONE, and an age that agrees with the one already held.

treeSays: Not in the tree at all
recordSays: BORN AT S. COSTANTINO, not at Zambrone or Briatico. His marriage act of 1824 makes him «di anni trentaquattro, NATO IN S. COSTANTINO, contadino, domiciliato in Zambrone» -- so the Ventrice came into Zambrone from San Costantino Calabro, a few kilometres away, and moved on to Briatico afterwards, where he died in 1831. HIS AGE IS ALSO IN DISPUTE WITH ITSELF: thirty-four in March 1824 gives 1790; thirty-three in June 1828 gives 1795. Both are his own declarations, five years apart in a man who could not write.

kind: Missing people — A WHOLE NEW YORK HOUSEHOLD
treeSays: Three children: Anna, Maria and an Antonio with no dates
recordSays: FOUR CHILDREN BORN IN MANHATTAN, none of them in the tree with a date and three of them not in it at all. ANTONIO b. 3 OCTOBER 1896; SERAFINA b. 15 AUGUST 1898; CLEMENTINA b. 21 DECEMBER 1900; and a SECOND ANTONIO b. 13 OCTOBER 1902. Every one names «father ROCCO ARENA, mother GENEROSA COSTA» -- the couple married at Scilla in December 1888. AND THE HOUSEHOLD HAS AN ADDRESS AT LAST: 141 MULBERRY STREET in 1896 and 1898, 198 MULBERRY by January 1901. That corroborates the Ellis Island manifest of 1899, which sends Giovanni Arena to «BROTHER ROCCO, N. YORK, MULBERRY ST» -- two independent sources, one street, and now a number. IT ALSO DATES THE CROSSING FROM THE INSIDE: Anna was born at Scilla in January 1893 and Antonio in Manhattan in October 1896, so the household moved between those dates, which fits the 1892 and 1894 crossings already documented.
source: New York Roman Catholic Parish Baptisms (Findmypast) — Our Lady of Loretto and Most Precious Blood

kind: a child who died, read from a repeated name
treeSays: Nothing — the tree has one Antonio and no dates
recordSays: TWO SONS NAMED ANTONIO, SIX YEARS APART. Rocco Arena and Generosa Costa baptised an Antonio on 15 November 1896 and another Antonio on 2 November 1902. IN THIS FAMILY'S PRACTICE THAT MEANS THE FIRST DIED and the name was given again. This archive has already read exactly this pattern once, at Scilla, where ORAZIO ARENA named two sons DOMENICO in 1856 and 1859 -- «the first child almost certainly died in infancy and the name was reused, which was ordinary practice». NO DEATH ACT HAS BEEN FOUND and none has been looked for. The inference rests on the custom and on the second baptism, which is why it is «inferred» and not «documented». What would settle it is a New York death or a burial record between 1896 and 1902.
source: New York Roman Catholic Parish Baptisms — two baptisms, 1896 and 1902

recordSays: BORN 20 DECEMBER 1900. The NAA's description of her alien passenger declaration gives the day: «CRUPI [MAZZA] Angela born 20 December 1900».
ARRIVED BRISBANE 7 DECEMBER 1937 ON THE VIMINALE, with two daughters -- «Maria age 15; Carmela age 8». The archive had no arrival for her and no idea the Mazza were in Australia this early.
BORN 20 FEBRUARY 1899. Given in the NAA's description of his internment dossier: «Prisoner of War/Internee: Mazza, Rosario; Date of birth - 20 February 1899; Nationality - Italian».

kind: Birth year and birthplace — A CONTRADICTION
recordSays: CANNOT BOTH BE TRUE. She arrives at Brisbane on 7 December 1937 as an ITALIAN ALIEN aged EIGHT -- so born about 1929, in Italy. A child born at Tully in 1926 would be eleven and an Australian-born British subject, needing no alien declaration at all. Her sister Maria, «age 15», fits the tree's 1922 exactly, so the record is not loose about ages.

DIED AT SCILLA ON 8 FEBRUARY 1932. Antenati's name index gives the act with both parents and his wife: «Padre Francesco Antonio, Madre Serafina Arlotta, Coniuge Generosa Costa» -- all three match this archive exactly, and he is the only Rocco Arena in the Scilla death index so described.
source: Antenati name index, Scilla, atto di morte 8 February 1932 (an_ud16599906 series)

recordSays: DIED AT SCILLA ON 31 MARCH 1936, «Padre Antonio, Madre Serafina Arlotta, Coniuge Concetta Russo». He sailed for New York in May 1899 to join his brother Rocco and he came home. This is the second half of the sojourning argument: he baptised no child in America because his wife never left Scilla, and neither did he, finally.
source: Antenati name index, Scilla, atto di morte 31 March 1936

kind: Death -- RETRACTED, and it was my own
who: Serafina Arena, born New York 1898 — the death withdrawn
recordSays: RETRACTED 17 SEPTEMBER. THE ACT IS NOT HERS. This row said she died at Scilla on 15 August 1912, on her fourteenth birthday, and the coincidence of dates was what made it persuasive. READING THE ACT ENDED IT: Scilla, Morti 1912, parte I, atto 83 records «e morta ARENA SERAFINA, DI MESI TRE, residente in Scilla, NATA IN QUESTO COMUNE, da ROCCO, marinaro, e da GENEROSA COSTA, casalinga». THREE MONTHS OLD AND BORN AT SCILLA. She is a LATER DAUGHTER OF THE SAME COUPLE, born about May 1912 and dead by August. WHAT MISLED ME: Antenati's name index gives «Nascita: Scilla» on every entry, and I treated that field as a default rather than a claim because it seemed too convenient. IT WAS A CLAIM AND IT WAS RIGHT. THE NEW YORK SERAFINA'S FATE IS UNKNOWN AGAIN -- she was baptised at Our Lady of Loretto on 15 August 1898 and this archive has nothing after that.
source: Scilla, Morti 1912, parte I, atto 83 — read in the original

treeSays: The oldest Polistena in the archive, with no parents at all
recordSays: HIS DEATH ACT NAMES BOTH. «Camillo Antonio Polistena, died Scilla 19 October 1924, Padre GIUSEPPE, Madre ANNA PONTILLO, Coniuge GIOVANNA ROMANO.» The Polistena quarter gains a generation.
source: Antenati name index, Scilla death acts — atto di morte 19 October 1924

kind: my own reading — a name in dispute, RESOLVED
who: Giovanna Pontillo — who is Giovanna ROMANO
treeSays: Giovanna Pontillo, wife of Antonio Polistena, daughter of Giuseppi Pontillo and Nunziatta Pontillo
recordSays: SHE IS GIOVANNA ROMANO, AND THE PONTILLO BELONGS TO HER MOTHER-IN-LAW. A FOURTH record now calls her Romano -- her husband's death act of 1924 gives «Coniuge Giovanna Romano», and their daughter Santa's of 1920 gives «Madre Giovanna Romano». The same act names the husband's own mother as ANNA PONTILLO. SO THE EXPORT TOOK THE HUSBAND'S PARENTS AND HUNG THEM ON THE WIFE: «Giuseppi Pontillo» is Camillo Antonio's father GIUSEPPE POLISTENA, and the Pontillo is his mother ANNA. That is why this archive could never find a Pontillo family behind her -- there is not one. Two asserted ancestors dissolve and two documented ones replace them.
source: Antenati name index, Scilla death acts — atto di morte 19 October 1924; and atto di morte 4 May 1920 (Santa Polistena)

recordSays: DIED AT SCILLA ON 10 MAY 1936, «Padre Domenico, Madre Nunziata Sofi, Coniuge Maria Sofi» -- all three matching this archive exactly. He was fifty-two on the New Orleans manifest of March 1908, sailing for Quincy, Florida; he came home and lived another twenty-eight years. THE LAST MAN ON THE DONATO LINE WHOSE END WAS UNKNOWN.
source: Antenati name index, Scilla, atto di morte 10 May 1936

recordSays: DIED 5 JANUARY 1933, not 1934. «Teresa Polistena, Padre Giovanni, Madre Annunziata Donato» -- her parents as the tree has them. The year is out by one.
source: Antenati name index, Scilla, atto di morte 5 January 1933

who: Santa Polistena, daughter of Camillo Antonio
treeSays: Not in the tree as a person of her own
recordSays: DIED AT SCILLA 4 MAY 1920, «Padre Camillo Antonio, Madre Giovanna Romano». NOTE WHAT FOLLOWS HER: Giovanni Polistena named a daughter SANTA in 1920. An aunt dies in the May and a niece takes her name in the same year, which is the naming custom working in front of us -- and a third witness that the mother was a Romano.
source: Antenati name index, Scilla, atto di morte 4 May 1920

kind: Relationship — AND IT MAKES THEM COUSINS
who: Anna Arlotta — Generosa Costa's mother and Serafina Arlotta's sister
treeSays: Two separate women of the same name, and the question left open
recordSays: THEY ARE ONE WOMAN, AND ROCCO ARENA MARRIED HIS FIRST COUSIN. FOUR ACTS NOW AGREE AND NONE CONTRADICTS. (1) ANNA ARLOTTA, died 16 March 1915: «Padre GIOVANNI ARLOTTA, Madre MARIA COSTA, Coniuge ANTONINO COSTA» -- and Giovanni Arlotta and Maria Costa are SERAFINA ARLOTTA'S OWN PARENTS, so Anna and Serafina were sisters. (2) ANTONINO COSTA, died 1 June 1915: «Coniuge ANNA ARLOTTA», confirming the couple from his side. (3) GENEROSA COSTA, died 6 June 1916: «Padre ANTONINO COSTA, Madre ANNA ARLOTTA» -- her own death act naming that same couple as her parents. (4) Scilla Matrimoni 1888 atto 63, which gave those parents in the first place. SO SERAFINA WAS ROCCO'S MOTHER, ANNA WAS GENEROSA'S MOTHER, AND THE TWO WERE SISTERS. UPGRADED FROM «probable» TO «certain» ON 16 SEPTEMBER, when the Costa side came in. WHAT WOULD STILL BREAK IT: two different couples named Giovanni Arlotta and Maria Costa at Scilla in the same decades. Nothing read so far suggests one, and four mutually consistent acts would all have to be pointing at the wrong pair.
source: Antenati name index, Scilla, atti di morte 16 March 1915, 1 June 1915 and 6 June 1916; against Scilla, Matrimoni 1888, atto 63

treeSays: No death, and no parents in the tree at all
recordSays: DIED AT SCILLA ON 6 JUNE 1916, «Padre ANTONINO COSTA, Madre ANNA ARLOTTA, Coniuge ROCCO ARENA». Her parents are exactly those the marriage act of 1888 gave, now from a second and independent document, and her husband is named. SHE DIED SIXTEEN YEARS BEFORE HIM: Rocco Arena followed her on 8 February 1932.
source: Antenati name index, Scilla, atto di morte 6 June 1916

treeSays: Known only as «Antonio Costa, b. c. 1840», with no parents
recordSays: DIED AT SCILLA ON 1 JUNE 1915, «Padre LORENZO COSTA, Madre GENEROSA POLISTENA, Coniuge ANNA ARLOTTA». TWO NEW ANCESTORS ON A LINE THAT STOPPED DEAD AT HIM. And the grandmother's name is the granddaughter's: GENEROSA POLISTENA to GENEROSA COSTA, which is the naming custom working exactly as it should and is a quiet corroboration of the whole chain.
source: Antenati name index, Scilla, atto di morte 1 June 1915

who: Anna Arlotta and Antonino Costa died eleven weeks apart
recordSays: ANNA ARLOTTA DIED 16 MARCH 1915 AND HER HUSBAND ANTONINO COSTA ON 1 JUNE 1915. Her act names her husband as Antonino Costa; his names his wife as Anna Arlotta. THE TWO ACTS CONFIRM EACH OTHER FROM OPPOSITE SIDES, which is what makes the couple safe to build on. Their daughter Generosa followed them in June 1916.
source: Antenati name index, Scilla, atti di morte 16 March and 1 June 1915

kind: my own reading — a name in dispute, SETTLED
who: Giovanna Romano, not Pontillo — her own death act
treeSays: Giovanna Pontillo, daughter of Giuseppi Pontillo and Nunziatta Pontillo
recordSays: HER OWN DEATH ACT ENDS IT. «GIOVANNA ROMANO, died Scilla 15 July 1930, Padre ANNUNZIATO, Madre ANGELA ZIRILLI, Coniuge CAMILLO ANTONIO POLISTENA.» She is named with her own surname, her own parents and her own husband, on her own act. THAT IS FIVE RECORDS CALLING HER ROMANO -- Scilla Nati 1883 atto 206, the New Orleans manifest of 1908, her husband's death act of 1924, her daughter Santa's of 1920, and now this. THE TREE'S «GIUSEPPI PONTILLO» AND «NUNZIATTA PONTILLO» ARE NOT HER PARENTS AND NEVER WERE. Her parents are ANNUNZIATO ROMANO and ANGELA ZIRILLI, and the Pontillo belonged to her mother-in-law, ANNA PONTILLO. Two asserted ancestors are withdrawn and two documented ones replace them.
source: Antenati name index, Scilla, atto di morte 15 July 1930

recordSays: BORN ABOUT 1844, NOT 1835. His death act of 19 October 1924 gives his age as EIGHTY -- «è morto Polistena Camillo Antonio, di anni ottanta, pescatore, residente in questo Comune, nato in Scilla». NINE YEARS OUT, and the archive's «about 1835» was a guess from his son's birth year rather than a record. The act is read, not indexed: Scilla, Morti 1924, parte I, atto 83.
PESCATORE -- a fisherman, like most of Scilla. Both declarants at his death were fishermen too: MATRA CAMILLO FU GIACOMO, sixty-three, and POLISTENA ANTONIO FU LUIGI, twenty-eight.

DIED AT SCILLA ON 19 OCTOBER 1924 AT FIFTY MINUTES PAST MIDNIGHT, at the house in RIONE MONACINA. The act was registered the same morning at twenty to nine. It names him «dal fu GIUSEPPE» and «dalla fu PONTILLO ANNA», both already dead, and «marito di ROMANO GIOVANNA» -- so his wife outlived him, as the index says she did, by six years.

treeSays: Not in the tree, and not provably his from the electoral roll
recordSays: SHE IS HIS WIFE, AND THE INTERNMENT FILE PROVES IT. The 1959 Queensland roll put a MARIO CRUPI and a MARIA CRUPI at Tully with the address column BLANK on both, and this archive expressly declined to pair them on that -- adjacency in an alphabetical roll proves nothing. THE SERVICE AND CASUALTY FORM SETTLES IT: «Marital Condition: Married. Next of Kin: MARIA CRUPI. Address of Next of Kin: P.O. Bemerside, Via Ingham. Relationship: WIFE.» AND IT DATES THE MARRIAGE. His naturalisation record of 26 April 1940 describes him as SINGLE; he is married by 20 April 1942. They married inside those two years.
source: NAA: MP1103/1, Q30124; against NAA: A714, 9/4300

recordSays: PESCATORE. His death act calls him a fisherman, as it calls both declarants and both witnesses. THE MAN WHO CROSSED THE ATLANTIC FOUR TIMES AND KEPT A HOUSEHOLD ON MULBERRY STREET DIED IN THE TRADE HE WAS BORN TO.

DIED AT VIA PROF. ZAGARI, SCILLA, AT A QUARTER PAST SIX IN THE EVENING ON 8 FEBRUARY 1932; the act was drawn the next morning at four minutes past ten. «dal fu FRANCESCO ANTONIO ... e dalla fu ARLOTTA SERAFINA ... VEDOVO DI COSTA GENEROSA.» A WIDOWER -- Generosa Costa died in June 1916 and he outlived her by fifteen years and eight months. The declarants were PONTILLO ROCCO FU GIOVANNI, sixty-five, and LAMERI GIUSEPPE FU LUIGI, eighty; the witnesses PONTILLO SANTO FU GIOVANNI, eighty-one, and ALFONZETTI ROCCO FU ANTONINO, fifty-nine. All fishermen, all illiterate.

HIS DEATH ACT MAKES HIM SEVENTY-ONE ON 8 FEBRUARY 1932, WHICH WOULD PUT HIS BIRTH BEFORE FEBRUARY 1861. The archive has his birth act as Scilla Nati 1861 ATTO 228 -- a high act number, so late in the year -- and the 1900 United States census gives «b. Sept 1861», which would make him SEVENTY, not seventy-one. ONE YEAR APART, AND THE BIRTH ACT WINS. An age on a death act is what two elderly neighbours told the registrar, not something read off a record; both declarants here were fishermen in their sixties and eighties and both signed with a mark. RECORDED BECAUSE IT IS THE KIND OF SMALL DISCREPANCY THAT LATER GETS «FIXED» IN THE WRONG DIRECTION.
source: Scilla, Morti 1932, parte I, atto 9; against Scilla, Nati 1861 atto 228 and the 1900 US census

recordSays: BORN ABOUT 1856, NOT 1851, AND TWO RECORDS AGREE AGAINST THE TREE. His death act of 10 May 1936 makes him «di anni OTTANTA»; the New Orleans manifest of March 1908 makes him FIFTY-TWO. Both point at 1855 or 1856. THE TREE'S 1851 WOULD HAVE MADE HIM EIGHTY-FIVE AT DEATH AND FIFTY-SEVEN ON THE SHIP. Five years out, and it matters because he is on the spine.
source: Scilla, Morti 1936, parte I, atto 20; against the New Orleans manifest of March 1908

recordSays: MARINAIO -- a mariner, not a fisherman. The distinction is worth keeping: his contemporary GIOVANNI ARENA, who died six weeks earlier and sixty yards away, is also «marinaio», while ROCCO ARENA four years before is «pescatore». Scilla's men went to sea two different ways.

DIED AT SIX IN THE MORNING ON 10 MAY 1936, AT VIA GROTTE 66, SCILLA. «e morto DONATO MICHELE, di anni ottanta, marinaio, residente in Scilla, nato in questo Comune, dal fu DOMENICO e da fu SOFI NUNZIATA, MARITO DI SOFI MARIA.» Both parents dead, HIS WIFE STILL LIVING. The declarants were LICO FRANCESCO DI DOMENICO, twenty-four, and PALAMARA GIOVANNI FU ANTONINO, thirty-seven, both day-labourers.
MARINAIO. His brother Rocco is «pescatore» on his own act of 1932 -- one a mariner, one a fisherman, which is a real distinction in a town like Scilla and not a scribal variant.

who: Giovanni Arena (Rocco's brother, b. 1854) — the act, read
recordSays: DIED AT NINE IN THE MORNING ON 31 MARCH 1936, AT VIA GROTTE 72, SCILLA. «e morto ARENA GIOVANNI, di anni OTTANTUNO, marinaio, residente in Scilla, nato in Scilla, dal fu ANTONIO e dalla fu ARLOTTA SERAFINA, MARITO DI RUSSO CONCETTA.» THE AGE IS EXACTLY RIGHT: born 30 April 1854, he was eighty-one and a month short of eighty-two. His wife CONCETTA RUSSO was still living, which is why she never appears in the Scilla death index -- she outlived the indexed span or died under a spelling not yet found.

who: Via Grotte — the Arena and the Donato were neighbours
recordSays: SIXTY YARDS AND SIX WEEKS APART. GIOVANNI ARENA died at VIA GROTTE 72 on 31 March 1936; MICHELE DONATO died at VIA GROTTE 66 on 10 May 1936. THE STREET WAS ALREADY IN THIS ARCHIVE AND NOBODY HAD PUT IT TOGETHER: Fortunato Arena was born at Via Grotte 70 in 1891, Giuseppe Arena at Via Grotte 75 in 1892, Maria Donato at Via Grotte 21 in 1888, and Giovanni Polistena at Via Grotte 47 in 1883. THREE OF THIS FAMILY'S FOUR SCILLA QUARTERS LIVED ON ONE STREET, which is how they kept marrying each other.
source: Scilla, Morti 1936, atti 14 and 20; against Nati 1891 atto 186, Nati 1892 atto 230, Nati 1883 atto 206

treeSays: Not in the tree; this archive had him last seen alive in November 1888 and no death
recordSays: DEAD ON 29 AUGUST 1901, at seven ten in the morning, in the house at VIA GROTTE NUMBER TWO, Scilla. Entered as ARENA FRANCESCO, di anni ottantadue, PESCATORE -- son of the late FILIPPO, pescatore, and of the late COSTA DOMENICA, filatrice, and MARITO DI ARLOTTA SERAFINA. All three of those identifiers are already in this archive from three separate acts, and no other man at Scilla carries them together. Declared by two becchini, Cesoriero Domenico, 46, and Fontana Ignazio, 52. He was born 25 November 1819, so he was eighty-one and nine months, not eighty-two; the rounding is the register's habit and the identification does not rest on the age. He was last seen alive in this archive on 18 November 1888, at the banns of his son Rocco. THIRTEEN YEARS OF HIS LIFE ARE NOW CLOSED, and his widow's death is fixed as later than his.

treeSays: Not in the tree; this archive had her alive in November 1888 and no death
recordSays: DEAD ON 24 APRIL 1908, at four in the morning, in the house at VIA GROTTE NUMBER TWO, Scilla — THE SAME ADDRESS AT WHICH HER HUSBAND DIED on 29 August 1901. Entered as ARLOTTA SERAFINA, di anni settantasette, FILATRICE, daughter of the late GIOVANNI, pescatore, and of the late COSTA MARIA, tessitrice, and VEDOVA DI ARENA ANTONIO. Born 13 June 1830, she was seventy-seven years and ten months — the register's figure is exact. She was a widow for six years and eight months, in a house her sons had left for America.

treeSays: No occupation; not in the tree
recordSays: TESSITRICE, a WEAVER — not a filatrice. Almost every woman in this register spins; Serafina Arlotta, her own daughter, is a filatrice. Her mother wove. Given in her daughter's death act of 24 April 1908, which also confirms her dead by that date and confirms the parentage that the marriage act of 1851 first gave.

kind: Method — a woman indexed under the wrong surname
treeSays: This archive assumed the annual index carries a woman under her maiden name
recordSays: IT DOES NOT ALWAYS. The 1908 annual index enters her as «ARENA Serafina, fu Giovanni» — her HUSBAND'S surname over her FATHER'S forename — while the act itself says ARLOTTA. Eleven A blocks were read looking for an Arlotta, and she was found only because Arena happens to be an A as well. THE RULE THAT FOLLOWS: when sweeping an annual index for a married woman, read the block for her husband's initial too, and treat a patronymic that fits as worth the download whatever surname sits in front of it.
source: Scilla, Morti 1908, parte I, atto 55 against the 1908 indice annuale

kind: Two women of one name — A GUARD, NOT A FINDING
who: Generosa Costa × the second Generosa Costa
recordSays: THERE ARE TWO AND THEY MUST NEVER BE MERGED. (1) GENEROSA COSTA, born about 1868, a filatrice, daughter of ANTONINO COSTA and ANNA ARLOTTA, married ROCCO ARENA at Scilla in December 1888, died at Scilla 6 JUNE 1916. She is on this archive's spine -- Anna Arena's mother. (2) A second GENEROSA COSTA, wife of PASQUALE DONATO, who died 20 April 1937; Pasquale is a son of DOMENICO DONATO and NUNZIATA SOFI, which makes him MICHELE DONATO'S BROTHER. So the two women sit one in each of this archive's two Scilla lines, the Arena and the Donato, and a tree that meets both will be tempted to fuse them. THE SEPARATION IS EVIDENCED, not assumed: the first was already dead in 1916, twenty-one years before the second's husband died, and their parents differ. COSTA AT SCILLA IS NOT A SMALL NAME -- the name index holds seventy-six Costa records and eighteen Costa deaths, including a THIRD Generosa in the previous generation, GENEROSA POLISTENA, for whom Rocco's wife was very likely named.
source: Antenati name index, Scilla — atti di morte 6 June 1916 and 20 April 1937

treeSays: Giovanna Romano has no siblings in the tree
recordSays: THREE SISTERS, each with her own death act naming the same parents -- ANNUNZIATO ROMANO and ANGELA ZIRILLI, who are Giovanna Romano's parents. MARIA ROMANO, d. 26 July 1917, wife of GIOVANNI CARDONA. CONCETTA ROMANO, d. 11 April 1926, wife of ROCCO DONATO. MARIANTONIA ROMANO, d. 24 June 1930, wife of MATTEO BOVA. Giovanna herself died 15 July 1930, seven weeks after Mariantonia. NOTE THE SECOND ONE. A Romano sister married a DONATO. Giovanna Romano married CAMILLO ANTONIO POLISTENA, and this archive's Donato and Polistena are already tied twice over. The Romano are a third strand in the same knot, and Concetta's husband Rocco Donato wants placing against Domenico Donato's household.
source: Antenati name index, Scilla — atti di morte 26 July 1917, 11 April 1926, 24 June 1930, 15 July 1930

kind: Missing people — GENEROSA COSTA'S UNCLES AND AUNT
who: The children of Lorenzo Costa and Generosa Polistena
treeSays: Lorenzo Costa and Generosa Polistena have no children in the tree but Antonino
recordSays: FOUR OF THEM, each named on his or her own death act as a child of LORENZO COSTA and GENEROSA POLISTENA -- Generosa Costa's paternal grandparents. ANTONIO COSTA, d. 1 JUNE 1915, husband of ANNA ARLOTTA: that is Generosa's own father, and the act is the first thing this archive has ever had that dates him. GIUSEPPE COSTA, d. 17 May 1915, sixteen days before his brother. MARIANA COSTA, d. 18 July 1922, wife of DOMENICO PONTILLO. DOMENICO COSTA, d. 8 September 1932, husband of CONCETTA ROMANO. AND THE NAMING CUSTOM LANDS AGAIN: Antonino Costa's first daughter is GENEROSA, for his own mother Generosa Polistena, exactly as the custom predicts. THE THIRD TIE: Mariana Costa married a PONTILLO and Domenico Costa married a ROMANO -- the two surnames that were in dispute over Camillo Antonio Polistena's wife. Scilla is a very small town.
source: Antenati name index, Scilla — atti di morte 17 May 1915, 1 June 1915, 18 July 1922, 8 September 1932

recordSays: MARIA PONTILLO, who died 14 OCTOBER 1922, daughter of GIUSEPPE PONTILLO and GIUSEPPA PALADINO. Domenico Arlotta is Serafina Arlotta's brother, so this is Rocco Arena's uncle by marriage. Her own death act names her parents, which puts two more Pontillo into the record.
source: Antenati name index, Scilla — atti di morte 14 March 1915 and 14 October 1922

kind: Two men of one name — A GUARD, NOT A FINDING
who: Antonio Arena × the other Antonio Arena
treeSays: One Antonio Arena married to a Serafina
recordSays: THERE ARE TWO AND THE WIVES SHARE A GIVEN NAME. (1) FRANCESCO ANTONIO ARENA, b. 25 November 1819, m. SERAFINA ARLOTTA at Scilla on 7 February 1851, d. 29 August 1901 at Via Grotte 2. This archive's direct line. THE REGISTERS DROP HIS FIRST NAME CONSTANTLY -- the acts of 1853, 1854 and 1861 call him plain ANTONIO, and so does his son Giovanni's death act of 1936 -- so he is ROUTINELY INDEXED AS «Antonio Arena, husband of Serafina». (2) ANTONIO ARENA, husband of SERAFINA DE LUCA, a proprietario, both dead by August 1895 when their son ORAZIO ARENA died at sixty-five; three more of their children are in the death index -- GRAZIA (d. 14 February 1913), ANNA (d. 8 March 1917, wife of Rocco Paladino) and ANNUNZIATA (d. 12 April 1919). SAME GIVEN NAME, SAME WIFE'S GIVEN NAME, SAME TOWN, SAME DECADES. Anyone sweeping «Antonio Arena + Serafina» merges two families. THE DISCRIMINATOR IS THE WIFE'S SURNAME -- ARLOTTA or DE LUCA -- and it must be read every single time, never inferred. THE SECOND ONE IS ALREADY A TRAP THIS ARCHIVE HAS SPRUNG: the Orazio Arena who died in 1895 was taken for the tree's Orazio Arena, the supposed father of Rocco, and he is not -- he is Antonio and Serafina DE LUCA's son. Different wife, different parents, different family.
source: Antenati name index, Scilla — atti di morte 14 February 1913, 8 March 1917, 12 April 1919; Scilla, Morti 1895 (Orazio Arena); Scilla, Nati 1819 atto 186 and Matrimoni 1851 atto 13

kind: Citation — the act number is wrong
treeSays: This archive cites «Scilla, Nati 1830 atto 2» in three places
recordSays: IT IS ACT 89, NOT ACT 2. The act itself, read as a certified copy in the marriage processetti of 1851, is headed «Num. d'ordine 89». «2» is a TAVOLA ROW NUMBER, taken for an act number -- the same mistake already recorded at Briatico, whose 1828 annual index runs one behind the register throughout. THE DATE IS RIGHT: 13 June 1830, at two in the night, in her parents' own house, declared by her father the next afternoon.
source: Scilla, Nati 1830 atto 89, read in Matrimoni processetti 1849-1852, fascicolo 13 of 1851

kind: Age — two of his own declarations, eleven years apart
treeSays: Born about 1779, from being seventy-five in April 1854
recordSays: HIS DAUGHTER'S BIRTH ACT MAKES HIM FORTY IN JUNE 1830, so born about 1790 -- ELEVEN YEARS LATER. Both figures are his own, given in person: in 1830 he declares Serafina's birth as her father, in 1854 he declares his grandson Giovanni's birth and is entered as «figlio del fu Domenico, di anni settantacinque, marinaro». Both call him marinaro; the 1830 act calls him «Sig.». NOT RESOLVED HERE, AND NOT AVERAGED. Either one declared age is badly out -- which this register does often enough -- or there are two Giovanni Arlotta and the 1854 declarant is not Serafina's father, which would cost this archive the Domenico Arlotta generation. THE TEST is his own marriage act to Maria Costa, before 1830, in the processetti of 1824-1827 or 1828-1831, which would give his age a third time and name his parents.
source: Scilla, Nati 1830 atto 89 against Nati 1854 atto 76

recordSays: A DOMENICO COSTA, COMMERCIANTE REGNICOLO, DI ANNI QUARANTASEI, stood as first witness at Serafina Arlotta's registration in June 1830 -- and the act says the witnesses were PRODUCED BY GIOVANNI ARLOTTA himself, which at Scilla means family. Forty-six in 1830 is a birth about 1784, which makes him twenty-three when Maria Costa was born about 1807. A father-in-law at his granddaughter's registration is the ordinary reading. IT IS A READING. Costa is one of the commonest surnames in the town -- seventy-six in the death index alone -- and this archive has already met a Domenica Costa, a Maria Costa, a Generosa Costa twice over and an Antonino Costa in four different households. The test is Giovanni Arlotta's marriage act, which names the bride's father outright.

kind: All four alive — inferred in the morning, CONFIRMED in the afternoon
who: Filippo Arena, Domenica Costa, Giovanni Arlotta and Maria Costa
treeSays: No date of any kind for three of the four
recordSays: THEY WERE ALL FOUR ALIVE ON 7 FEBRUARY 1851 -- read from an absence, and graded accordingly. The marriage processetti of Francesco Arena and Serafina Arlotta run to FOUR SHEETS: the two birth acts, the notification without opposition, and the certificate of the canonical celebration. NO DEATH ACT OF ANY PARENT IS BOUND IN. The same office, in fascicolo 3 of the same year, bound in «Atto di morte del padre e dell'avo paterno dello Sposo» -- so it did include them when a parent or grandparent was dead. CAVEAT: Serafina was twenty and needed parental consent, and no consent sheet is listed either, so consent was given in person rather than on paper; an argument from a four-line index is weaker than an act, and this is graded as inferred for that reason. UPGRADED THE SAME DAY, AND BY A POSITIVE READING RATHER THAN AN ABSENCE. The ANNUAL MARRIAGE TAVOLA for 1851 names both spouses' parents AND MARKS THE DEAD WITH «FU» -- the 1828 Tavola writes Giovanni Arlotta's father as «FU Dom.co» beside his living mother «Barbaro Anna», and «fu» appears on this very page of 1851 in other entries. ENTRY 1 OF THE 1851 TAVOLA IS «ARENA FRANCESCO e ARLOTTA SERAFINA», and its parents are written «FILIPPO, e COSTA DOMENICA» and «GIOVANNI e COSTA MARIA» -- NEITHER WITH «FU». So all four were living when their children married, and this is no longer an argument from a four-line index.
source: Scilla, Matrimoni processetti 1849-1852, fascicolo 13 of 1851, against fascicolo 3 of 1851; Scilla, Matrimoni 1851, Tavola annuale, entry 1, against the same page's «fu» entries

treeSays: Nothing but a Queensland death registration
recordSays: INTERNED. His aliens registration card is stamped LOVEDAY 35924 on the front, and the CHANGE OF ADDRESS panel on the reverse records him moved «ex Gay[thorne] to 14A» on 16 MARCH 1943 and «Released and returned to Queensland» on 22 OCTOBER 1943. THAT IS THREE MEN IN THIS FAMILY INTERNED IN THE SAME EIGHTEEN MONTHS: ROSARIO MAZZA, who married Angela Crupi; MARIO CRUPI, at Loveday 18 August 1942 to 30 December 1943; and now ANTONINO CRUPI, her other brother. The internment of Italian-Australians was not a thing that happened to one member of this family. AND THE CENSOR PRESERVED A SENTENCE OF HIS. The card carries a mail extract dated 2 APRIL 1943, from a letter to his wife in Queensland: «... Our freedom will come soon and we shall always cry Vive Italia.» It is the only sentence in this archive spoken by Antonino Crupi, and it exists because an official copied it out as evidence against him.
source: NAA: D4028, CRUPI ANTONIO (item 9209610), both sides

recordSays: HE DID NOT NEED ONE. NAA: BP4/3, ITALIAN CRUPI P records «Alien Registration Certificate NOT ISSUED», with the folio noting that CRUPI WAS NATURALISED 23 FEBRUARY 1932. The D4028 series registers ALIENS; by 1939 Pietro Crupi was a British subject and fell outside it. An absence that is explained is worth as much as a card -- and it dates his naturalisation, which this archive did not have.

BOTH ON THE OTRANTO, INTO BRISBANE ON 19 AUGUST 1930. NAA: BP9/3 ITALIAN CRUPI P and ITALIAN CRUPI A are consecutive entries in the Brisbane aliens register and both give that ship and that date; Pietro is entered as born 1898, Antonino as born 1907. Antonino's own card gives his ENTRY as 2 SEPTEMBER 1930, a fortnight after the ship docked -- the same split between a ship's arrival and a man's registered entry already recorded for the passenger index. BOTH DATES ARE TRUE and they answer different questions. Their brother MARIO came two years earlier, on the MARIA CRISTINA into Brisbane on 20 MAY 1928.
source: NAA: BP9/3 ITALIAN CRUPI P, CRUPI A and CRUPI M; NAA: D4028 CRUPI ANTONIO and CRUPI MARIO

kind: Two men of one name — A GUARD, NOT A FINDING
who: Antonino Crupi × the Antonio Crupi of Serrata
treeSays: One Antonio Crupi with a D4028 card
recordSays: THERE ARE TWO, AND THEIR BARCODES ARE CONSECUTIVE. NAA: D4028 item 9209610 is CRUPI ANTONIO, born PIEDIMONTE ETNEO, arrived BRISBANE 2 September 1930 -- Angela Crupi's brother. NAA: D4028 item 9209609 is ALSO CRUPI ANTONIO, born SERRATA, arrived MELBOURNE 20 October 1926 -- Serrata is in Calabria, six hundred kilometres from Piedimonte, and he is nobody here. Item 9209611 is MARIO CRUPI, also Piedimonte, also this family. So the run 9209609 / 9209610 / 9209611 is stranger, brother, brother. ADJACENCY IN AN ALPHABETICAL CARD SERIES IS NOT KINSHIP -- the same lesson the Queensland electoral rolls taught when consecutive roll numbers were read as a household. THE DISCRIMINATOR IS THE BIRTHPLACE and it must be read every time.

ANTONINO CRUPI naturalised 7 NOVEMBER 1946, born 1907 at Piedimonte, then RESIDENT AT TULLY, Queensland, WIFE NELLIE (NAA: A714 57/18792). MARIO CRUPI naturalised 26 APRIL 1940, born 1905, resident at INGHAM, entered as SINGLE (NAA: A714 9/4300). PIETRO CRUPI naturalised 23 FEBRUARY 1932 (NAA: BP4/3). ONE CONFLICT LEFT OPEN: Antonino's aliens card of October 1939 already says MARRIED, and this archive notes an Antonino Crupi marrying in Queensland on 24 AUGUST 1940. Either that marriage belongs to another man of the name, or the word «married» was added to the card after 1939. Not resolved.
source: NAA: A714 57/18792; A714 9/4300; BP4/3 ITALIAN CRUPI P

kind: Identification — the roll could not settle it and a naturalisation did
treeSays: Two Antonio Crupi on the 1959 Queensland roll and no way to choose
recordSays: HE IS THE TULLY MAN. NAA: A714 57/18792 records «CRUPI, Antonio; naturalised 7 NOVEMBER 1946; place of birth PIEDIMONTE, Italy; year of birth 1907; PLACE OF RESIDENCE: TULLY, QLD; [W] CRUPI, NELLIE». Piedimonte and 1907 tie it to the aliens card of Angela Crupi's brother; TULLY and NELLIE tie it to the 1959 electoral roll, where an ANTONIO CRUPI, cane farmer, shares DEAN STREET, TULLY with a NELLIE CRUPI. The other Antonio Crupi of that roll, a farmer at SILKWOOD EAST in the Innisfail sub-district, is a different man. THE ROW NAMED ITS OWN TEST -- «a wife to match against Nellie Crupi» -- and a document found while reading his brother's aliens card supplied it. Nothing here rests on the roll's ordering, which this archive has already been burned by once. AND HE MOVED. The aliens card of October 1939 gives him at INGHAM, a boot repairer; by 1946 he is a cane farmer at Tully, where Pietro and Mario also were. ONE THING TIDIED. The Queensland marriage of an Antonino Crupi on 24 AUGUST 1940 sat awkwardly against a card registered in October 1939 that already says MARRIED. The card carries annotations from 1943, so «married» was very probably written on it after the fact; the 1940 marriage is the likelier date and is very likely to Nellie. Stated as the reading it is.
source: NAA: A714 57/18792; NAA: D4028 CRUPI ANTONIO (item 9209610); Australia Electoral Rolls 1959, Herbert, Tully sub-district

kind: Port — the ship's first landfall is not where he got off
recordSays: HE GOT OFF AT BRISBANE, ON 21 OCTOBER 1957. NAA: BP25/1, ITALIAN PROSTAMO F -- the BRISBANE aliens registration series -- reads «Prostamo, Francesco - Nationality: Italian - arrived BRISBANE on the T/v ROMA 21 OCTOBER 1957». BOTH DATES ARE TRUE AND THEY ANSWER DIFFERENT QUESTIONS: 10 October is when the ROMA first touched Australia at Fremantle, which is what the passenger index records; 21 October is when this man walked down the gangway, eleven days and three ports later. THE SECOND IS THE ONE THAT MATTERS, because the family settled in Queensland and the Brisbane series is where he registered. The same correction applies to FRANCESCA PROSTAMO, who travelled with him: NAA: BP25/1, ITALIAN TRUNGADI F, same ship, same 21 October, same port. This is the third time this archive has met the pattern -- it was proved on a K269 manifest where an unlabelled letter column turned out to be the port of debarkation.
source: NAA: BP25/1, ITALIAN PROSTAMO F (item 5067016) and ITALIAN TRUNGADI F (item 5080545)

kind: A married surname, not a second woman
treeSays: Francesco Prostamo's daughter, born 1945 at Briatico, twelve on the voyage
recordSays: THE NATIONAL ARCHIVES CATALOGUES HER AS «TRUNGADI [nee PROSTAMO], FRANCESCA». That is her Brisbane aliens registration, same ship and same day as her father. A TWELVE-YEAR-OLD IS NOT «NEE» ANYTHING, and the manifest -- read in the original -- gives her age as twelve and her birth as 1945 at Briatico. The reading that fits both is that the registration CARD was annotated with her married name years after 1957 and the catalogue transcribed the card's final state, which is exactly what an aliens card is for. SO TRUNGADI IS A SURNAME TO GO LOOKING FOR -- a Queensland marriage, a later address -- AND NOT A SECOND WOMAN TO ADD. Recorded as a lead.
source: NAA: BP25/1, ITALIAN TRUNGADI F (item 5080545), against the K269 manifest of the ROMA

treeSays: Their marriage is not documented anywhere in this archive
recordSays: A COMMONWEALTH FILE NAMES THEM AS HUSBAND AND WIFE. NAA: J25 1971/3900, held at Brisbane, 1953-1971: «ARENA, ROCCO; WIFE ANGELINA [OR ANGELA] [NEE POLISTENA]». J25 is the Queensland immigration and naturalisation correspondence series, and its file titles name a couple together with the WIFE'S MAIDEN NAME -- which is exactly what was missing. IT DOES NOT DATE THE MARRIAGE. What it does is turn «undocumented» into «documented as a fact, undated», and name the file that may date it. The file is «not yet examined», which means nobody has ever asked; an access examination is free and takes about ninety days. Michael's grandparents on the Arena side.

kind: A second migration, twenty years and half a world apart
treeSays: One crossing: Palermo to New Orleans, 1908
recordSays: HE MAY HAVE GONE TO AUSTRALIA TOO. NAA: BP9/3, ITALIAN POLISTENA G -- the Brisbane aliens register -- reads «Polistena, GIOVANNI BORN 1883 - nationality Italian - arrived in BRISBANE on the ORMONDE 21 FEBRUARY 1928». This archive's Giovanni Polistena was born at Scilla in 1883 (act 206), sailed from PALERMO to NEW ORLEANS on the LIGURIA in February 1908 on the line immediately after Michele Donato, married Michele's daughter Nunziata about 1916, and named a daughter Santa at Scilla in 1920. A crossing to Brisbane in 1928 sits after all of that and would explain how this family reached Queensland at all. THE YEAR OF BIRTH MATCHES EXACTLY AND THE PORT IS THE RIGHT ONE. IT IS STILL A CANDIDATE: the register entry carries no parents and no birthplace, and POLISTENA is a comune in Reggio Calabria as well as a surname, so the name alone proves nothing. The test is the item itself, or any Queensland record placing him there in the 1930s.

treeSays: Two Donato-Polistena marriages, a generation apart
recordSays: SIX, ACROSS TWO COUNTRIES. Four at Scilla, from the death index: Maria Donato x Giuseppe Polistina (she d. 1911); Raffaele Polistena x Teresa Donato, three of whose children die there; Giovanni Polistena x Annunziata Donato; and Nunziata Donato x Giovanni Polistena about 1916. TWO MORE IN QUEENSLAND, from the National Archives: NAA J25 1967/9873, «Polistena, Giuseppe; wife MARIA MADDALENA [nee DONATO]», and NAA J25 1970/3023, «DONATO, CONCETTA [nee POLISTENA]». TWO FAMILIES THAT INTERMARRY SIX TIMES OVER TWO GENERATIONS AND TWO HEMISPHERES ARE NOT TWO FAMILIES WHO HAPPENED TO MEET. They were one neighbourhood at Scilla -- Via Grotte -- and they were still one neighbourhood in Brisbane.
source: Antenati name index, Scilla; NAA: J25 1967/9873 and 1970/3023

kind: A surname that is also a town — A GUARD
recordSays: IT IS ALSO A COMUNE IN THE PROVINCE OF REGGIO CALABRIA, seventy kilometres from Scilla, and THIS FAMILY IS FROM SCILLA. A name search on POLISTENA in the National Archives returns four A714 naturalisations for men called OLIMPIO, MARFEA, FOGLIADORO and PALESTRI whose PLACE OF BIRTH is Polistena, and three A7919 prisoner-of-war files -- SAVARESE, ROSSI, BOTTIGLIERI -- for men born there and captured in Africa. Seven of fifty results are the town wearing the family's name. ANY SWEEP ON THIS SURNAME MUST READ THE FIELD, not the word: a Polistena in the SURNAME column is a candidate, a Polistena in the BIRTHPLACE column is a stranger from the same province. The same caution will apply to any Italian surname that is also a place.
source: NAA NameSearch, POLISTENA, all record categories — 50 items

treeSays: Married a Prostamo; his name unknown
recordSays: DOMENICO FRANCESCO PROSTAMO. NAA: J25 1962/5930, Brisbane, 1952-1966: «PROSTAMO, Domenico Francesco; wife ASSUNTE MARIA [NEE MELLUSO]». She was born about 1936 to GREGORIO MELLUSO and CARMELA MARIA BORELLO and buried at Mount Gravatt in October 1991 under a Prostamo surname that nobody here could attach to a man. Here he is. The file is «not yet examined» and would very likely give the marriage date, both their arrivals, and where they lived.

kind: Household — a family Queensland's index could not show
treeSays: One Melluso registration in the whole Queensland index, so no siblings and no children
recordSays: HIS HOUSEHOLD IS IN A COMMONWEALTH FILE. NAA: J25 1972/23086, Brisbane, 1959-1974: «MELLUSO, GREGORIO; WIFE CARMELA; AND CHILDREN GIUSEPPE, MARIA [SURNAME PROSTAMO]». «Wife Carmela» is CARMELA MARIA BORELLO, already known from his daughter's death registration. WHAT IS NEW IS A SON, GIUSEPPE. AND THE BRACKET IS AMBIGUOUS, deliberately left so: a DAUGHTER Maria carrying the surname Prostamo is just Maria Assunta married to Domenico Francesco Prostamo; a SON Giuseppe carrying it cannot be, and would mean Carmela brought Prostamo children into the marriage with her. THE FILE TITLE IS A FINDING AID, NOT A RECORD, and this archive has been caught by one before. Opening it settles which; it is «not yet examined», so an access examination is free.

kind: Age — my own entry, corrected the same day
recordSays: BORN ABOUT 1802. She is TWENTY-SIX at her own marriage on 30 August 1828, with her father Rocco Costa and her mother Pasqualina Idone standing beside her and giving formal consent. THIS ARCHIVE WROTE «c. 1807» EARLIER THE SAME DAY, off her daughter's birth act of 1830, which makes her twenty-three. A woman's own marriage act, sworn in her parents' presence, outranks her husband's statement at a registration desk five years later. The old figure is left on the record rather than replaced silently, because the size of the gap -- five years -- is itself information about how much these declared ages can be trusted.
source: Scilla, Matrimoni 1828 atto 28, against Nati 1830 atto 89

kind: Marriage — the other Antonio Arena, documented at last
who: Antonio Arena and Serafina De Luca
treeSays: Two men of one name, separated only by a caution
recordSays: THEY MARRIED AT SCILLA ON 10 AUGUST 1828, ATTO 26. The annual Tavola names all four parents: HIS are ORAZIO ARENA and LETTERIA MORABITO; HERS are FILIPPO DE LUCA and ANNA ALFONZETTI. THIS CLOSES THE COLLISION WITH A DOCUMENT INSTEAD OF A WARNING. This archive's Francesco Antonio Arena married Serafina ARLOTTA in February 1851 and was the son of Filippo Arena and Domenica Costa; this Antonio Arena married Serafina DE LUCA in August 1828 and was the son of Orazio Arena and Letteria Morabito. Different decade, different parents, different wife's family. AND IT EXPLAINS THE NAME THAT CAUSED THE TROUBLE: their son ORAZIO ARENA, who died at Scilla in August 1895 and was once taken for the tree's Orazio, is named for HIS OWN GRANDFATHER, exactly as the custom predicts.

kind: Method — the marriage Tavola is a life-status snapshot
treeSays: An index that gives a name and a number
recordSays: IT GIVES FOUR PARENTS AND TELLS YOU WHICH OF THEM WERE DEAD. Scilla's «TAVOLA annuale alfabetica dei Matrimonj» carries the columns Num. d'ordine | Cognomi e Nomi degli Sposi | Patria | Professione | COGNOMI E NOMI DE' GENITORI | Giorno della Celebrazione -- and the parents column uses the Italian convention: «FU X» where the parent is dead, a bare forename where the parent is living. The 1828 Tavola writes Giovanni Arlotta as son of «FU Dom.co e Barbaro Anna»: father dead, mother alive, in four words. ONE INDEX OPENING THEREFORE DATES THE LIFE STATUS OF FOUR PEOPLE AT A SINGLE MOMENT, without opening an act. That is a better instrument than this archive has been treating it as, and it applies to every year of the restaurazione series. CAVEAT: the date column is the CHURCH celebration, not the civil act -- in 1828 the Tavola says 7 September where the civil promise was 30 August -- so an act number and a Tavola date will not agree, and neither is wrong.

kind: Missing people — a sister found in somebody else's index
treeSays: Rocco Costa and Pasqualina Idone have one child in this archive
recordSays: CANDIDA COSTA, who married GIOVANNI VILARDI at Scilla in 1811. The annual marriage Tavola names her parents as «ROCCO e PASQUALINA IDONE» -- the same Rocco Costa and Pasqualina Idone who stood at MARIA COSTA'S wedding in August 1828 and consented in person. SO CANDIDA IS MARIA'S SISTER, and Serafina Arlotta's aunt. Her husband's parents are GAETANO VILARDI and ANTONIA MELLICA. SHE WAS FOUND IN AN INDEX OPENED FOR SOMEBODY ELSE -- the 1811 Tavola was being read for Filippo Arena, who is not in it. A marriage Tavola that names four parents will keep doing this, which is an argument for reading the whole section rather than scanning for one surname.

kind: Dated at last — a roll line becomes a man
treeSays: A timber cutter at Cardwell on the 1959 electoral roll, and nothing else
recordSays: NATURALISED IN QUEENSLAND ON 27 NOVEMBER 1934. NAA: BP4/3, ITALIAN MAZZA A, held at Brisbane. Naturalisation of that period wanted about five years' residence, SO HE WAS IN AUSTRALIA BY ABOUT 1929 -- thirty years before the roll that found him, and long before the post-war migration this archive has been reading him against. He also died in Queensland on 31 JULY 1975, registration 1975/C/4171, whose index entry gives his father only as «Mazza» and no mother at all. SO HE IS NOW A MAN WITH THREE DATES AND STILL NO PARENTS, and he is still NOT a documented relative. What would settle it: his death certificate, which names parents where the index does not; or the naturalisation file itself, which carries a birthplace -- and if that birthplace is PIEDIMONTE ETNEO this becomes a different question entirely.
source: NAA: BP4/3, ITALIAN MAZZA A (item 5237835); Queensland death registration 1975/C/4171

treeSays: Interned; the dossier is known and nothing after it
recordSays: HE WENT INTO THE CIVIL ALIENS CORPS. NAA: J1737, MAZZA R: «Mazza Rosario, CAS 15000 - CIVIL ALIENS CORPS (CAC)», Brisbane, 1944, ACCESS OPEN. The CAC was the labour corps that interned Italians were released into rather than freed -- road and timber work under military administration -- and CAS 15000 is his service number in it. This archive had his internment dossier, MP1103/1 Q8110, and then a silence. IT ALSO SITS BESIDE THE OTHER TWO. Mario Crupi was at Loveday from August 1942 and released on 30 December 1943; Antonino Crupi came out on 22 October 1943. Rosario's Corps file is 1944. The three men were moving through the same system within months of each other.
source: NAA: J1737, MAZZA R (item 6305636); against NAA: MP1103/1, Q8110

kind: Internment — the dossier, and the number that proves it
treeSays: Interned at Loveday, known only from the aliens card
recordSays: HIS DOSSIER IS NAA: MP1103/1, Q7838 — «Prisoner of War/Internee: Crupi, Antonio; Date of birth - 05 November 1907», Melbourne, 1942-1943, access OPEN, with a companion at MP1103/2, Q7838. AND THE NUMBER IS THE PROOF. His aliens registration card, NAA: D4028, carries «Q. 7838» written beside his name. The same serial in two unrelated series — the Queensland aliens register and the Commonwealth internee dossiers — ties the card and the camp to one man, and the identification no longer rests on birthplace alone. MARIO CRUPI'S DOSSIER DOES THE SAME: MP1103/2, Q30124, against the «N.B.E. certificate Q30124» on his own card. ONE FIGURE IN CONFLICT AND LEFT SO. The card says «5.10.07», which is 5 OCTOBER 1907. The dossier catalogue says 05 NOVEMBER 1907. A month apart, both Commonwealth paperwork about the same man, and the dossier itself is what would settle it.
source: NAA: MP1103/1 Q7838 (item 8621112) and MP1103/2 Q7838 (item 9909834); against NAA: D4028, CRUPI ANTONIO

kind: A third man of the name — A GUARD
who: Antonino Crupi × the Antonio Crupi of Victoria
recordSays: THERE IS A THIRD. NAA: MP1103/1 and MP1103/2, PWV11028 — «Prisoner of War/Internee: Crupi, Antonio; Date of birth - 10 JANUARY 1904» — a VICTORIAN internee, the PWV prefix against our Q for Queensland, and three years older. THIS ARCHIVE HAS NOW SET ASIDE THREE MEN CALLED ANTONIO CRUPI: the Serrata-born holder of aliens card 9209609, one barcode from Antonino's; the Silkwood East farmer on the 1959 electoral roll; and this Victorian internee. EACH WAS EXCLUDED BY A DIFFERENT FIELD — birthplace, address, and the state prefix on a serial number. The name alone has never once been enough.

kind: A fourth internment that is NOT this family — A GUARD
who: Rocco Arena × the interned Rocco Arena
treeSays: Three men of this family interned in 1942-43
recordSays: A ROCCO ARENA WAS INTERNED IN AUSTRALIA AND HE IS NOT ONE OF THEM. NAA: MP1103/1 and MP1103/2, PWN9406, give «Prisoner of War/Internee: Arena, Rocco; Date of birth - 31 AUGUST 1909»; A367 C18000/298 and C329 42 are his Aliens Tribunal objection, number 35 of 1941; C123 4326 and C123 ITALIAN INTERNEES [Box 611] are Sydney lists of 1940; ST1233/1 N35192 is «Rocco Arena [Interned] [Application for Naturalisation]». THE ARITHMETIC EXCLUDES HIM ABSOLUTELY. This archive's ROCCO ARENA ARRIVED IN AUSTRALIA ON 27 DECEMBER 1953 -- thirteen years after that man was interned. The other Rocco Arena, born at Scilla in 1861, DIED THERE ON 8 FEBRUARY 1932. Neither was in New South Wales in 1940. THIS GUARD EXISTS BECAUSE THE PATTERN IS ALREADY SET. Rosario Mazza, Mario Crupi and Antonino Crupi were all interned, all documented this week, and a fourth man of the right surname in the same camps would be very easy to believe. He is a Sydney man born in 1909 and he is nobody here.
source: NAA: MP1103/1 PWN9406; A367 C18000/298; ST1233/1 N35192; against NAA passenger index, arrival 27 December 1953

kind: A structural finding about the thinnest quarter
treeSays: One of this archive's four Scilla families
recordSays: THEY ARE BARELY IN THE BIRTH REGISTERS OF THE 1830s. Three complete annual P sections -- 1834, 1835 and 1836 -- cover 629 BIRTHS AND HOLD EXACTLY ONE POLISTENA. The P section at Scilla in those years is Paladino, Pirrotta, Patafio, Papalia, Pizzarello, Parisi, Piria. THE POLISTENA ARE NOT AN OLD SCILLA SURNAME AT THAT DATE. WHICH MAY BE WHY THIS QUARTER STOPS. The Polistena line reaches Camillo Antonio, born about 1835, and above him only his parents' names off a death act. If the family came INTO Scilla rather than being of it, the generation above will be in another comune's registers -- and POLISTENA IS ITSELF A COMUNE in the province of Reggio Calabria, seventy kilometres away, which is exactly where a surname like that comes from. Recorded as a reading of an absence, not a finding, and the test is whether Camillo Antonio's birth act exists at Scilla at all.
source: Scilla, Nati 1834, 1835 and 1836, Tavole annuali — complete P sections

kind: A lead with the wrong surname on it — OPENED, AND THE INDEX WAS THE LIAR
treeSays: Camillo Antonio Polistena has no documented siblings
recordSays: «POLISTINA ANNUNZIATA, DI GIUSEPPE E MARTELLO ANNA» -- entry 191 of the 1836 Scilla birth Tavola, born 2 DECEMBER 1836, and the ONLY Polistena birth in three years of that register. THE GIVEN NAMES ARE RIGHT AND THE SURNAME IS NOT. Camillo Antonio Polistena's death act of 1924 gives his parents as GIUSEPPE POLISTENA and ANNA PONTILLO. Here the mother is ANNA MARTELLO. THREE READINGS AND NO DECISION: the Tavola is wrong; the death act is wrong; or these are two different couples who each happen to pair a Giuseppe with an Anna. TWO THINGS MAKE THE FIRST WORTH TESTING. The Tavola is an INDEX, and this archive has already been caught by one -- the 1854 index that called Serafina Arlotta «Rosa» and briefly turned a brother into a cousin. AND FOUR ENTRIES EARLIER, at 168, stands «PONTILLO GIOVANNI, di Giuseppe e Paladino Giuseppa» -- a Pontillo household with a Giuseppe at its head, in the same section of the same page. A clerk copying down that column had both surnames under his hand. ACT 191 OF 1836 SETTLES IT AND IS THREE IMAGES AWAY. OPENED THE SAME HOUR. ACT 204 OF 1836 -- not 191; the Tavola's «Num. d'ordine» is an index row and this index carries NO act number at all. Scilla, 2 DECEMBER 1836: the midwife TERESA ARENA, forty-four, declared a girl born that morning at eight to ANNA PONTILLO, THIRTY-FIVE, lawful wife of GIUSEPPE POLISTINA, THIRTY-EIGHT, MARINARO, and named ANNUNZIATA POLISTINA. THE MOTHER IS PONTILLO. The Tavola's «Martello» is wrong, the death act of 1924 is right, and ANNUNZIATA IS CAMILLO ANTONIO POLISTENA'S SISTER -- the first sibling he has ever had here. The guess about WHY the index erred also held: four entries earlier in the same P section stands «Pontillo Giovanni, di Giuseppe e Paladino Giuseppa».
source: Scilla, Nati 1836, Tavola annuale, entry 191; Scilla, Nati 1836 atto 204, read in the original

kind: Dated at last — the Polistena get their first two birth years
treeSays: Two names off a death act, with no dates and no trades
recordSays: GIUSEPPE POLISTENA WAS THIRTY-EIGHT AND A MARINARO, ANNA PONTILLO THIRTY-FIVE, in December 1836 -- so born about 1798 and about 1801. Given in their daughter Annunziata's birth act, Scilla atto 204 of 1836. THE POLISTENA QUARTER HAD NO DATED ANCESTOR ABOVE CAMILLO ANTONIO AT ALL; it now has two, with a trade. AND THE TRADE MATTERS: a MARINARO sets the Polistena beside the Arena and the Arlotta as a third Scilla sailing family, against the Mazza, who were contadini in Sicily.

kind: Method — an index with no act number in it
treeSays: The Tavola's «Num. d'ordine» points at the act
recordSays: IT DOES NOT, IN 1836. That Tavola's columns are Num. d'ordine | Cognomi e Nomi dei Nati | Cognomi e Nomi dei Genitori | GIORNO DELLA NASCITA -- and THERE IS NO ACT-NUMBER COLUMN. The «Num. d'ordine» is the INDEX ROW, running 1 to 222 across the alphabet. Entry 191 is a Polistina; ACT 191 of the register is a SQUILLACI birth at Solano on 9 November. THE ONLY KEY FROM THIS INDEX INTO THIS REGISTER IS THE DATE OF BIRTH, and the acts run in date order -- which found act 204 in two probes. This is the Briatico 1828 trap in a harder form: there the index ran one behind the register, here it does not point at the register at all.
source: Scilla, Nati 1836, Tavola annuale against atti 191 and 204

kind: Age — wrong by at least six years, and eleven years prove it
treeSays: Born about 1835, from being forty-eight in September 1883
recordSays: HE IS NOT IN THE SCILLA BIRTH REGISTER FOR 1833, 1834, 1835, 1836, 1837 OR 1838. Six consecutive complete P sections. AND HIS PARENTS ARE IN TWO OF THEM: GIUSEPPE POLISTENA and ANNA PONTILLO have a son ROCCO on 13 DECEMBER 1833 and a daughter ANNUNZIATA on 2 DECEMBER 1836. THE THREE YEARS BETWEEN HOLD NO POLISTENA BIRTH AT ALL, and they are not thin years -- 201, 206 and 222 births. A child born to this couple about 1835 is simply not there. SO «FORTY-EIGHT» IN SEPTEMBER 1883 IS OUT BY AT LEAST TWO YEARS, and he was born BEFORE 1833 or AFTER 1838. Declared ages in this register are routinely a year out; this one is worse. THE SEARCH MOVES TO 1830-1832 AND 1839-1840, and it should not stop at the first year that fits. EXTENDED TO ELEVEN YEARS, 1830-1840, AND THE DIRECTION IS NOW FIXED. His parents' children come in DECEMBER 1833, DECEMBER 1836 and JANUARY 1840 -- three years apart, twice, with 1830, 1831 and 1832 read and empty of them. SO ROCCO IS THE ELDEST AND CAMILLO ANTONIO CANNOT BE EARLIER; he must be 1841 OR LATER, and «forty-eight» in September 1883 is wrong by at least SIX years. THE NAMING CUSTOM AGREES: a first son takes the father's father's name, making Giuseppe's father a ROCCO POLISTENA, and a later son takes the mother's father's -- which would make CAMILLO ANTONIO the namesake of a CAMILLO PONTILLO. Anna Pontillo was about thirty-five in 1836 and could bear to about 1846, so the window is 1841-1848.
source: Scilla, Nati 1830-1840, Tavole annuali — eleven complete P sections

kind: Missing people — two siblings for the thinnest quarter
treeSays: Camillo Antonio Polistena has no siblings in the tree
recordSays: HE HAS TWO. ROCCO POLISTINA, born 13 DECEMBER 1833, and ANNUNZIATA POLISTINA, born 2 DECEMBER 1836 -- both children of GIUSEPPE POLISTENA and ANNA PONTILLO, the couple named on Camillo Antonio's own death act of 1924. Annunziata's act has been read in the original (Scilla, atto 204 of 1836) and gives her parents' ages: Giuseppe thirty-eight, Anna thirty-five. Rocco is so far only an index line. NEITHER IS IN THE FAMILY TREE, and until today this quarter had no documented person at Camillo Antonio's own generation beside him.
source: Scilla, Nati 1833 Tavola entry 144; Nati 1836 atto 204

kind: A second Polistena household — A GUARD
recordSays: THERE ARE AT LEAST TWO. The 1839 birth Tavola, entry 153, gives «POLISTINA MARIA -- FRANCESCO e LONGARDO GIUSEPPA -- 30 Maggio». That is not GIUSEPPE POLISTENA and ANNA PONTILLO, this archive's couple, and the child is not a sibling of Camillo Antonio. IT MATTERS BECAUSE THE SURNAME IS SO RARE HERE. Seven consecutive years of the Scilla birth register -- 1833 to 1839, about 1,450 births -- hold exactly FOUR Polistena, and three of them belong to these two couples. With a surname that scarce, the temptation to join any two bearers is strong and it should be resisted: the discriminator is the MOTHER, and here it is Longardo against Pontillo. NOTED AND NOT CONCLUDED FROM: LONGARDO is the surname of NATALINA LONGORDO, mother of the Filippo Arena who died at Scilla in 1915 and who was briefly taken for Rocco Arena's brother. The two spellings are one Scilla surname. AND THEY WERE THERE BEFORE THIS ARCHIVE'S COUPLE. The 1832 Tavola, entry 152, gives «POLISTINA DOMENICA -- FRANCESCO e LONGORDO GIUSEPPA -- 17 Dicembre». So Francesco and Giuseppa had a daughter in December 1832 and another in May 1839, while Giuseppe and Anna Pontillo had theirs in December 1833 and December 1836. TWO HOUSEHOLDS RUNNING IN PARALLEL FOR EIGHT YEARS, and between them they account for EVERY Polistena birth at Scilla in that time -- five in about 1,630 births.

kind: Missing people — a third child, and the shape of the family
treeSays: Camillo Antonio Polistena has no siblings in the tree
recordSays: FORTUNATA POLISTINA, born 28 JANUARY 1840 to GIUSEPPE POLISTENA and ANNA PONTILLO -- the 1840 Tavola, entry 107, which spells the mother PONTILLO correctly. SHE IS THE THIRD SIBLING FOUND TODAY, after Rocco (13 December 1833) and Annunziata (2 December 1836). AND THE THREE OF THEM GIVE THE FAMILY A SHAPE. Children in December 1833, December 1836 and January 1840 -- THREE YEARS APART, TWICE -- with 1830, 1831, 1832, 1834, 1835, 1837, 1838 and 1839 all read and holding no child of theirs. That is a regular household, and it means Rocco is the eldest and Camillo Antonio is younger than all three.

kind: Three Polistena households, not one — THE MAP
treeSays: A surname with one household behind it
recordSays: THREE, AND ELEVEN YEARS OF THE BIRTH REGISTER NAME ALL OF THEM. GIUSEPPE POLISTENA x ANNA PONTILLO -- this archive's -- with Rocco (1833), Annunziata (1836) and Fortunata (1840). FRANCESCO POLISTINA x GIUSEPPA LONGARDO, with Salvadore (1830), Domenica (1832) and Maria (1839). LUIGI POLISTINA x MARIANNA (or GIOVANNA) BAVIERA, with Antonino (1830) and Francesco Antonio (1831). EIGHT BIRTHS IN ABOUT 2,100. The surname is scarce enough that any two bearers look related and rare enough that the temptation to join them is strong. THE DISCRIMINATOR IS THE MOTHER, every time: Pontillo, Longardo, Baviera. NOTE ONE TRAP IN PARTICULAR: Luigi's son born 21 June 1831 is called FRANCESCO ANTONIO POLISTINA. That is one word away from CAMILLO ANTONIO POLISTENA, in the right town in the right decade, and it is a different child of different parents. It would be very easy to seize on.
source: Scilla, Nati 1830-1840, Tavole annuali — eleven complete P sections

kind: A Giuseppe and an Anna Pontillo who are NOT these two — A GUARD
treeSays: One couple at Scilla answering to «Giuseppe e Anna Pontillo»
recordSays: THERE ARE TWO, AND THE OTHER IS A PALMISANO. The 1841 Scilla birth Tavola, entry 160: «PALMISANO GIO. BATTISTA -- GIUSEPPE e ANNA PONTILLO -- 26 Agosto». This archive's couple are GIUSEPPE POLISTENA and ANNA PONTILLO, whose children appear in the same register in 1833, 1836 and 1840. SAME TWO GIVEN NAMES, SAME DISTINCTIVE MAIDEN SURNAME, SAME TOWN, SAME DECADE. WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN AN ORDINARY COLLISION: the way this archive has been searching these Tavole is by READING THE PARENTS COLUMN for «Giuseppe e Pontillo Anna». That method walks straight into this entry and cannot tell the difference, because the thing that separates them is the CHILD'S SURNAME -- the column a parent-scan skips. IT IS NOT DECIDED HERE whether this is a second Anna Pontillo or the same woman remarried; nothing in the index says. It is written down so that the next person reading these pages checks the first column before celebrating.

FOUR. The 1842 birth Tavola, entry 145: «POLISTINA SALVADORE -- DOM.co e COSTA CATERINA -- 12 Gennaro». Added to GIUSEPPE x ANNA PONTILLO, FRANCESCO x GIUSEPPA LONGARDO and LUIGI x MARIANNA BAVIERA. Thirteen years of the Scilla birth register now name four distinct couples of this surname and nine children between them. NOTE THE WIFE'S SURNAME: COSTA, which is the third time a Costa woman has married into a family this archive is tracking at Scilla -- after Domenica Costa to Filippo Arena and Maria Costa to Giovanni Arlotta. Costa is simply a very common Scilla surname and no connection is claimed.
